Home/IoT sensors/Soil sensor

Wireless soil sensors.
Understand the root zone.
Plan the next action.

Hitelecom H Series wireless soil sensors bring soil moisture, EC, pH and NPK readings from selected monitoring points into your project. Soil temperature can be included where confirmed in the selected configuration. Match the sensing channels, probe arrangement and medium to your crop, planting or maintenance objective, then choose a 4G, NB-IoT or LoRa variant and reporting profile. Product form and probe options can be customized, with data delivered to Hitelecom Cloud or an agreed receiving platform.

SENSING & INSTALLATION

Measure the soil at a defined point.
Keep the installation practical.

Plan locations around representative soil, planting type, irrigation zones and the effective root area. Agree depths and probe contact for the selected medium, and use separate identified points where comparisons are needed. Protect the sensing elements and cables from field operations. Confirm the communication terminal's mounting and network coverage, with access for inspection and project verification.

FROM SOIL READING TO SITE ACTION

See the soil trend.
Give the team a useful next step.

A sampling interval defines when measurements are taken; a reporting interval defines when data is sent. Choose these separately around the expected soil changes, irrigation events and operational workflow. Reporting intervals can be configured for the project. Verify the required data and notification timing during commissioning.

01

Measure

The selected channels record conditions at a defined soil point. Agree the sensing depth, medium, sampling interval and reference checks before deployment.

02

Transmit

Readings follow the selected 4G, NB-IoT or LoRa path. Confirm local coverage, the reporting profile and delivery to the receiving platform.

03

Review

Compare soil trends with rainfall, irrigation and maintenance records. Set project thresholds and agree who reviews a notification or visits the site.

REPORTING & POWERLow-power planning for field deployment.

The published H Series reference is more than 10 years of battery life at a four-hour reporting interval under specified test conditions. Review the estimate for the selected sensing configuration and actual deployment. Measurement demand, sampling duty, network coverage, retransmissions, operating temperature and reporting frequency affect runtime. Agree the power arrangement and monitoring profile with the ordered specification.

01Field crops & irrigation5 monitoring tasks +

Follow root-zone wetting and drying across cultivated fields. Match monitoring points to crop rows, soil layers and irrigation blocks, recording the growing stage and field operations.

Row-crop irrigation blocks

Wetting response and drying between irrigation events at a defined crop-row position.+

Follow root-zone moisture through the irrigation cycle in maize, soybean or other row crops. Position representative points within each management block, then compare wetting and drying with irrigation records and crop stage. Where soil texture or elevation changes, give those zones their own reference rather than blending them into one average. The resulting time series supports a practical review of watering timing and field visits.

Measurements to observe
Wetting response and drying between irrigation events at a defined crop-row position.
Monitoring point
Representative rows within each soil and irrigation block, at depths selected for the crop stage.
Placement & installation
Maintain soil contact and route cables clear of cultivation and harvest paths. Position the wireless terminal for reception and maintenance access.
Project details
Crop, soil texture, irrigation layout, root-zone depths, field operations and required reporting.

Rainfall-related wetting and subsequent drying in selected planted soil zones, with comparison to rainfall events, visible ponding and establishment watering records.
Monitoring point
Select representative planted soil in the lower receiving area and, where useful, a higher margin. Record each point's depth and position relative to the inlet.
Placement & installation
Install with consistent contact in the selected soil or verified planting medium. Preserve the garden's drainage features and protect equipment from sediment-clearing and planting work.
Project details

Monitoring selected root-zone locations creates a record of these differences through wet and dry weather. Compare moisture changes with rainfall, maintenance observations and planting condition to guide inspections and establishment care. Map every point to the swale layout so that repeated observations refer to the same planted area and soil depth.

ANSWERS FOR YOUR PROJECT

Frequently asked questions.

Practical answers for selecting soil channels, planning representative monitoring points and connecting the readings to planting and maintenance decisions.

Ask about your project ↗
Which soil parameters can I include in an H Series configuration?+

Start with the channels your project needs. The published soil family lists soil moisture, EC, pH and NPK measurement, with parameter combinations and probe options available for customization. Soil temperature is included where confirmed in the selected configuration. Ask for a channel list that identifies what each ordered unit measures, together with its range, measurement basis, probe arrangement and verification method for the intended soil or growing medium.

How does soil moisture monitoring support irrigation scheduling?+

A defined soil point shows how moisture changes after irrigation or rainfall and during the interval before the next event. Review that trend alongside soil texture, the effective root zone, crop or planting stage and recent weather. Establish the site's normal wetting and drying behaviour before setting an irrigation trigger. Combining the readings with watering records and field observations helps the team review timing and follow up areas that need attention.

Where and how deep should a soil probe be installed?+

Choose positions that represent the soil, planting and irrigation zone you want to observe. The depth should relate to the effective root area and the question being asked; separate identified points can compare upper and lower soil conditions where useful. Install the selected probe with consistent contact in the verified medium, and document its position. Include protected cable routes, maintenance access and the communication terminal's mounting in the deployment plan.

How many monitoring points does my site need?+

Plan the point count around meaningful differences in soil, crops or planting, irrigation zones, exposure and root depth. Begin with representative locations for the management questions your team needs to answer, then use an initial deployment to review whether more points would improve the picture. Keep a register of each point's soil and installation details. This makes comparisons useful and gives the quotation a clearer basis than a fixed number per area.

Can I use the same configuration in mineral soil and growing media?+

Select the configuration for the material it will measure. Mineral soil, peat, coco coir and other growing media can differ in structure, water retention and electrical response. Share the medium specification and expected conditions so probe suitability, measurement basis and site verification can be agreed. Establish a baseline in the actual material, with consistent probe contact and reference checks, before comparing readings across different beds, containers or substrate types.

How should I set a soil moisture alert?+

Build the threshold around your site's soil and planting needs. Record the moisture response through representative watering, rainfall and drying periods, and relate it to root-zone observations and the agreed irrigation strategy. Use that baseline to choose a practical notification level, then define who reviews the alert and what field check follows. Review settings as crops, seasons or soil management change, and verify the complete notification path during commissioning.

What do soil EC and pH readings help me understand?+

EC adds information about the medium's electrical conductivity, while pH describes its acidity or alkalinity. Review these trends together with moisture conditions, the selected measurement method and appropriate soil tests. Specify the EC range your site requires: the published standard channel is 0–1,000 µS/cm. Record the method used when comparing sensor and laboratory results, so the team interprets changes on a consistent basis for the intended planting or management objective.

How should NPK readings fit into a nutrient-management programme?+

Use the selected NPK channels within a documented soil-management plan. Agree which nutrient measurements are reported, their method and the reference tests used to check them in the actual soil. Compare trends with samples from representative locations, crop needs and the site's previous nutrient applications. Regional soil-test recommendations and the agronomist's plan provide the basis for fertilizer decisions, while the monitoring record adds context between field visits and scheduled sampling.

Can the sensor support parks, street trees and roadside planting?+

Yes, defined points in planted soil can support the maintenance team's view of root-zone moisture between visits. Select representative tree pits, lawn areas, shrub beds or planted medians, and connect the trends with watering routes, rainfall and plant inspections. For new trees, the root ball and surrounding soil may warrant separate observations. Specify installation depth, equipment protection and maintenance access so the record remains useful through establishment care and routine landscape work.

For ancient and veteran trees, a qualified tree-care specialist should select monitoring positions and approve installation within the root protection plan.

Can soil monitoring support rain gardens and permeable-pavement sites?+

Plan readings in verified soil or planting medium at clearly defined locations. For rain gardens and bioretention beds, compare wetting and drying trends with rainfall, visible ponding and maintenance inspections. Beside permeable paving, choose planted root-zone soil or a project-validated underlying soil point with consistent probe contact, rather than open gravel voids. Agree the medium and installation details before deployment, and use separate inspections or tests for the surface infiltration objective.

Which wireless option and platform should I specify?+

Choose the connection around coverage at the terminal position, the reporting requirements and the receiving platform. The published family lists 4G Cat.1, NB-IoT and LoRa variants, with Hitelecom Cloud and private-platform integration. Confirm regional modem support and the agreed message format. For LoRa, include the gateway, radio protocol and server path in the quotation. Check the full data route and terminal mounting before completing the field installation.

What information helps Hitelecom configure and quote my project?+

Share the application, soil or growing-medium specification, crop or planting type and the root-zone positions you want to observe. Add the required channels and ranges, point quantity, probe and cable arrangement, terminal mounting and available wireless coverage. Include sampling and reporting requirements, the receiving platform and any reference-testing needs. A planting plan, soil-test report or site section helps the team define a suitable configuration and prepare a quotation around your actual project.
